extracted.intended_audience: ICLR 2026 reviewers (and other conference reviewing participants such as Area Chairs and Senior Area Chairs)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines and required components for reviewers evaluating submissions to ICLR 2026, including ethical and LLM-related policies, review form components, and consequences for low-quality or noncompliant reviews. Targets timely, substantive peer reviews for conference papers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timely reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers are asked to provide timely ... reviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timely, high quality reviews are essential to the peer review process. Timeline dates are provided (bidding, writing reviews, discussion period) and reviewers should meet these deadlines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Substantive reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers are asked to provide ... substantive reviews and follow the reviewing guidelines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviews should be substantive (not placeholders). The Review Form Components (summary, strengths/weaknesses, scores, recommendation, confidence, questions, limitations and ethics flags) indicate expected content depth.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quantity requirement: three quality reviews per paper
rubrics_metrics.description: ICLR will be looking for 3 quality reviews per paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Area Chairs rely on multiple independent substantive assessments; reviewers contribute to meeting this per-paper target.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences for low-quality reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: Low quality reviews (e.g., placeholder reviews) will be flagged by Area Chairs and Senior Area Chairs, and flagged reviewers will be warned and urged to update the review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers who do not respond to these warnings will be liable to having their own papers desk rejected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adherence to the ICLR Code of Ethics
rubrics_metrics.description: All ICLR participants, including reviewers, are required to adhere to the ICLR Code of Ethics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers must follow the conference's ethical rules in conduct, conflicts of interest handling, and review content; see the Code of Ethics for specifics.

rubrics_metrics.name: LLM usage disclosure and reviewer responsibility
rubrics_metrics.description: If a reviewer uses an LLM, they must disclose this and are ultimately responsible for the LLM's outputs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disclosure is mandatory; reviewers remain accountable for any content generated or assisted by LLMs and must verify accuracy and appropriateness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on false/misleading claims and data fabrication
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether or not reviewers use LLMs, they must not make false or misleading claims, fabricate or falsify data, or misrepresent results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This applies to reviewers' written content as well as authors: reviewers should flag suspected fabrication/misrepresentation and avoid introducing such errors themselves (per LLM policy clause).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reciprocal review policy (access conditional on completing reviews)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers who are also authors will not see reviews of their own submissions during the rebuttal period until they complete their assigned reviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If reviews are late, reviewers and their co-authors will lose access to their paper reviews until completion. This enforces timely completion of assigned reviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strict rule: undisclosed LLM use leads to rejection
rubrics_metrics.description: Papers (or reviews) using LLMs without disclosure face immediate rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ICLR 2026 enforces one of the strictest policies for AI-generated content disclosure; failure to disclose LLM use risks immediate rejection of the paper (and reviews).

rubrics_metrics.name: Review component: summary of contributions
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviews should include a summary of contributions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a concise description of the paper's claimed contributions so Area Chairs and authors understand the reviewer's interpretation of the work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review component: strengths and weaknesses
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviews should include strengths and weaknesses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain positive aspects and limitations; be specific and evidentiary where possible to support scores and recommendations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review component: soundness score
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviews should include a soundness score.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess technical correctness, experimental validity, and methodological rigor; justify the numeric score with concrete critiques or supporting observations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review component: presentation score
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviews should include a presentation score.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate clarity, organization, readability, and completeness of exposition; note missing explanations, ambiguous notation, or poor figure/table quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review component: contribution score
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviews should include a contribution score.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess originality, novelty, and significance of the paper's contributions relative to the field; provide comparisons to prior work as rationale.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review component: overall recommendation
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviews should include an overall recommendation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Give a clear recommendation (e.g., accept/reject or numeric equivalent) informed by the scores and written critique.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review component: confidence
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State the reviewer's self-assessed confidence in their evaluation (e.g., familiarity with the topic, ability to judge experiments).

rubrics_metrics.name: Review component: questions for authors
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviews should include questions for authors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pose clarifying questions or requests for additional details that authors should address in rebuttal or revision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review component: limitations and ethics flags
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviews should include limitations and ethics flags.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Flag potential ethical concerns, limitations in the work (e.g., societal impact, bias, safety), and any other issues that merit attention by Area Chairs and authors.
